title: Rabbi Yosi bar Huna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Sanhedrin 105b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.105b) attributes to him the famous saying that Ruth was the daughter of Eglon, the grandson of Balak king of Moab. The reading should be Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina, as the saying appears in [Nazir 23b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.23b) and [Horayot 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.10b). In [Sotah 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.47a) it is attributed to Rabbi Yosi ben Choni; that is also the reading of Dikdukei Soferim in Sanhedrin.[^1][^2]

notes.text: ב״ב של means “grandson of”: Eglon, not Ruth, is the grandson in the Sanhedrin saying. דק״ס abbreviates Dikdukei Soferim. The proposed change of attribution is Hyman’s textual judgment.

The parallels differ in both attribution and genealogy. Nazir and Horayot attribute the saying to Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Chanina and call Ruth Eglon’s granddaughter. Sanhedrin attributes it to Rabbi Yosi bar Huna and calls Ruth Eglon’s daughter and Eglon Balak’s grandson. Sotah attributes it to Rabbi Yosi ben Choni and calls Ruth Eglon’s daughter and Eglon Balak’s son.
